title: Principles of Deliberate Practice on the Job
coreMove: Carve one repeatable subskill out of live work and install feedback close enough to alter the next attempt.
sourcePressure: The chapter transfers deliberate-practice logic into messy workplaces through subskill isolation, designed feedback loops, review habits, and self-diagnosis without pretending work is a clean training field. Frozen sidecar for chapter 5 contains no traceable named figure, study, place, date, or artifact beyond the authors and chapter mechanism; sourceAnchors stays empty rather than inventing one.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version says a busy job, annual review, or generic lesson learned meeting is workplace practice.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person 'You' direct address, retrospective 'It took her three weeks to see', question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

exampleSpecs.domain: hotel front-desk check-in recovery after double bookings
exampleSpecs.audience: a supervisor who sees apologies as personality rather than a trainable sequence
exampleSpecs.stakes: a guest can leave angry before the room problem is solved
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Emily replays one tense check-in, isolates the first apology sentence, and has the clerk practice that line with a new room option before the next guest arrives
exampleSpecs.firstImage: key cards fanned beside a red overbooking alert

exampleSpecs.audience: an inspector whose reports keep missing the decision-relevant measurement
exampleSpecs.stakes: a contractor can keep working from a vague note that should have stopped the pour
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Daniel compares three old inspection notes, circles the missing measurement line, and writes the next site note on a template before leaving the slab
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a concrete slump cone rinsed beside a clipboard

exampleSpecs.audience: a producer whose guests keep giving rehearsed answers
exampleSpecs.stakes: the segment loses live discovery because one question type keeps closing the room
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Margaux clips twelve seconds of a flat answer, rewrites only the question opener, and tests the replacement on the next pre-interview call
exampleSpecs.firstImage: audio waveforms glowing above a cold studio fader

exampleSpecs.domain: restaurant expeditor ticket-call clarity during dinner rush
exampleSpecs.audience: a line leader whose shouted calls create repeated wrong plates
exampleSpecs.stakes: one allergy modification could get lost in noise
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: At 7:36 p.m., Mikkel marks each misheard allergy call on the rail, switches to a fixed call-back phrase, and checks whether the next three tickets come back clean
exampleSpecs.firstImage: order tickets clipped above a heat lamp with one allergy note underlined

exampleSpecs.audience: a librarian who keeps giving long answers before finding the real need
exampleSpecs.stakes: patrons leave with sources that do not match their assignment
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You watch Catarina save three transcript snippets, notice where she skipped the clarifying question, and script one shorter triage prompt for the next desk hour
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a receipt printer curling search terms beside a library keyboard

exampleSpecs.audience: a crew lead turning installation errors into a short practice loop
exampleSpecs.stakes: a misplaced rail can waste daylight and damage a roof membrane
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Aman photographs the last bad layout, has the apprentice mark the rail line on a mock shingle board, and compares it with the roof plan before climbing again
exampleSpecs.firstImage: chalk rail lines crossing a black mock shingle board

skillTargets: design fast feedback inside live work
choose self-diagnosis when no coach is available

tryThisNowSpec: Before the next repeated work action, name the smallest piece that failed last time. Create one feedback trace: recording, sample, checklist mark, peer note, or before-after comparison.
